newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian bond yields up, shorts outperform again.
newsitem.headline: Australian bond yields up, shorts outperform again.

text.p: *Australian bond yields closed higher, primarily in response to weakness in the U.S., although the short end outperformed once again and is still benefitting from last week's rate cut.
*U.S. faces durable goods orders, 2-year note sale.
Australian bond yields closed higher, primarily in response to weakness in U.S. Treasuries, although the short end outperformed once again and was still benefitting from last week's rate cut.

"The three-year part of the curve has seen another solid performance. With low inflation expected to stay, and still a large (yield) margin over cash, people believe the market can go further," one trader said.
Talk of a new bond issue for offshore markets also helped the short end, which saw the three-year yield spread to the U.S. go negative and the yield curve extend its recent steepening.
However, the long end was dogged by the U.S. sell-off which followed a sharp rise in consumer confidence and sparked renewed concern of Fed tightening.
Traders said there is also a feeling that the 10-year yield compression to the U.S. has gone as far as it can for now after brushing a three-year low of around 75 basis points last week.

Thursday sees the release of first quarter business inventories and April balance of goods and services, but the main event on the data front will be April retail trade on Friday for a more up to date indication of demand.
Short Canadian debt was undermined by fears of a Fed tightening, while New Zeland bonds held their ground, helped by talk issuance of Eurokiwi or samurai bond issues.
U.S. Treasuries face April durable goods orders and a A$16.5 billion two year note auction later on Wednesday.

The June three-year bond contract matched Friday's post-rate cut high of 93.60 in early trading, but is now back in a 93.52/93.57 range. Major resistance is seen at this year's 93.65 peak, analysts added.
